def load() -> pd.DataFrame:
    import glob
    import pandas as pd

    paths = [
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2002.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2003.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2004.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2005.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2006.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2007.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2008.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2009.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2010.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2011.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2012.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2013.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2014.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2015.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2016.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2017.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2018.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2019.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2020.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2021.csv",
        "data/environment/input/water-body-testing-2022.csv",
    ]

    matched = []
    for p in paths:
        ms = glob.glob(p)
        if not ms:
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"No files matched: {p}")
        matched.extend(ms)

    dfs = []
    for p in sorted(set(matched)):
        df = pd.read_csv(p)
        df["sourceFile"] = p.split("/")[-1]
        dfs.append(df)

    out = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True, sort=False)
    return out

operators.customDisplayName: Load and vertically concatenate water-body-testing yearly CSVs for 2002-2022: read each file via pd.read_csv (comma delimiter, header inferred), add provenance column 'sourceFile' (basename), and concat into one table.

def process(waterBodyTestingAll):
    import pandas as pd

    df = waterBodyTestingAll.copy()

    # Focus years requested; dataset currently spans 2002-2022 (inclusive)
    df = df[(df['Year'] >= 2002) & (df['Year'] <= 2023)]

    # Marine beaches only
    df = df[df['Beach Type Description'].astype(str).str.strip().str.lower() == 'marine']

    # Normalize violation flag to boolean exceedance
    v = df['Violation'].astype(str).str.strip().str.lower()
    exceed = v.eq('yes')

    # Exclude unknown / missing / other tokens from denominator
    valid = v.isin(['yes', 'no'])
    rate = exceed[valid].mean() * 100  # percent

    return pd.DataFrame([{
        'marineExceedanceRatePercent': rate,
        'nSamplesMarineValid': int(valid.sum()),
        'nExceedMarine': int(exceed[valid].sum()),
        'minYear': int(df['Year'].min()) if len(df) else None,
        'maxYear': int(df['Year'].max()) if len(df) else None,
    }])

operators.customDisplayName: Compute historical exceedance rate for marine beaches (2002-2023 inclusive): filter Year between 2002 and 2023; filter Beach Type Description == 'Marine' (case/whitespace-insensitive); normalize Violation to lowercase tokens; treat 'yes' as exceedance and 'no' as non-exceedance; exclude other/missing Violation values from denominator; return single-row table with exceedance rate as percent plus sample counts and min/max year coverage.
